guide_line: Count electron regions to get the electron-pair geometry, then ignore lone pairs to name the molecular shape. A molecule is polar only when its bond dipoles do not cancel.
steps: An electron region is a bond or a lone pair on the central atom. A double bond or a triple bond counts as one region.

Regions stay as far apart as they can. Two regions are linear (180°). Three are trigonal planar (120°). Four are tetrahedral (109.5°). Five are trigonal bipyramidal (90° and 120°). Six are octahedral (90°).
The electron-pair geometry counts every region. The molecular shape counts only the atoms. Lone pairs change the shape name.
Four regions: 0 lone pairs is tetrahedral, 1 is trigonal pyramidal, and 2 is bent. Three regions with 1 lone pair is also bent. Five regions: 1 lone pair is seesaw, 2 is T-shaped, and 3 is linear.
A bond is polar when the two atoms differ in electronegativity. The molecule is polar when those bond dipoles do not cancel.

Identical outer atoms on a symmetric shape cancel: linear CO2, trigonal planar BF3, tetrahedral CH4 and CCl4, trigonal bipyramidal PCl5, and octahedral SF6. A bent or pyramidal molecule, or a tetrahedron with different outer atoms, does not cancel.

worked_example.q: What is the molecular shape of CH4, and is the molecule polar or nonpolar?
steps: Carbon has four single bonds and no lone pair, so there are four regions.
Four regions and no lone pairs give a tetrahedral shape. The angle is 109.5°.
The four C–H bonds are arranged evenly, so the dipoles cancel.

similar_problem.q: What is the molecular shape of H2O?
similar_problem.hint: Oxygen has two bonds and two lone pairs. Name the shape from the atoms only, after the lone pairs have pushed them together.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of H2O?
problems.why: Oxygen has two bonds and two lone pairs, four regions in all. The electron-pair geometry is tetrahedral. The two atoms and the oxygen make a bent molecular shape.
hints: Oxygen has two bonds and two lone pairs. Name the shape from the atoms only, after the lone pairs have pushed them together.

problems.q: What is the electron-pair geometry of H2O?
problems.why: Two bonds plus two lone pairs are four regions. Four regions take a tetrahedral electron-pair geometry, even though the molecular shape is bent.
hints: Count lone pairs as regions for this question. Two bonds and two lone pairs are four regions around oxygen.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of NH3?
problems.why: Nitrogen has three bonds and one lone pair. Four regions give a tetrahedral electron-pair geometry. Leaving the lone pair out of the shape name gives trigonal pyramidal.
hints: Nitrogen has three N–H bonds and one lone pair. The lone pair is not an atom, so the shape is a three-sided pyramid.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of CH4?
problems.why: Carbon has four bonds and no lone pair. The molecular shape matches the electron-pair geometry: tetrahedral.
hints: Carbon in CH4 has four bonds and no leftover pair. The shape name matches the four-region geometry.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of BF3?
problems.why: Boron has three bonds and no lone pair. Three regions lie in a plane, so BF3 is trigonal planar.
hints: Boron in BF3 has three bonds and no lone pair. Three regions with nothing left over stay flat.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of CO2?
problems.why: Each C=O double bond is one region, and carbon has no lone pair. Two regions point opposite each other, so CO2 is linear.
hints: Count each C=O double bond as one region. Carbon has two regions and no lone pair.

problems.q: What is the bond angle in CH4, in degrees?
problems.why: CH4 has four bonding regions and no lone pair. The tetrahedral angle is 109.5°.
hints: CH4 is the four-region shape with no lone pairs. Use the ideal tetrahedral angle, including the decimal.

problems.q: What is the bond angle in CO2, in degrees?
problems.why: CO2 has two regions and no lone pair. The atoms lie on a straight line, so the angle is 180°.
hints: CO2 has only two regions around carbon. Two regions form a straight line.

problems.q: Is CO2 polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: Each C=O bond is polar, but the molecule is linear. The two bond dipoles point opposite ways and cancel, so CO2 is nonpolar.
hints: The C=O bonds are polar, but they lie on a straight line. Ask whether those two arrows cancel.

problems.q: Is H2O polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: Each O–H bond is polar, and the molecular shape is bent. The bond dipoles both point toward oxygen and do not cancel, so water is polar.
hints: The shape is bent, not linear. The two O–H dipoles point toward oxygen and do not sit opposite each other.

problems.q: Is CH4 polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: The four C–H bonds point to the corners of a tetrahedron. Equal bonds in that shape cancel, so CH4 is nonpolar.
hints: Four identical bonds point to the corners of a tetrahedron. That arrangement cancels.

problems.q: Is CH3Cl polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: CH3Cl is tetrahedral, but one outer atom is chlorine instead of hydrogen. The C–Cl dipole is not matched on the opposite side, so the molecule is polar.
hints: The shape is still tetrahedral, but chlorine replaced one hydrogen. The four directions are no longer the same bond.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of SF6?
problems.why: Sulfur has six bonds and no lone pair. Six regions give an octahedral molecular shape.
hints: Sulfur in SF6 has six bonds and no lone pair. Six regions take the octahedral arrangement.

problems.q: Is SF6 polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: Each S–F bond is polar. Opposite bonds in the octahedron point in opposite directions and cancel, so SF6 is nonpolar.
hints: Every S–F bond is polar. In an octahedron each bond has a partner pointing the opposite way.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of SF4?
problems.why: Sulfur has four bonds and one lone pair, five regions. The electron-pair geometry is trigonal bipyramidal. With one lone pair, the molecular shape is seesaw.
hints: SF4 has four bonds and one lone pair, which is five regions. One lone pair on that geometry leaves a seesaw of atoms.

problems.q: What is the electron-pair geometry of XeF2?
problems.why: Xenon has two bonds and three lone pairs. Five regions take a trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry.
hints: Add the bonds to the lone pairs on xenon. Two bonds plus three lone pairs are five regions.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of XeF2?
problems.why: The three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of the trigonal bipyramid. The two fluorine atoms are left opposite each other, so the molecular shape is linear.
hints: The three lone pairs take the equatorial spots. The two fluorines remain opposite one another.

problems.q: Is NH3 polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: Nitrogen is more electronegative than hydrogen, and the shape is trigonal pyramidal. The bond dipoles and the lone pair point the same general way, so NH3 is polar.
hints: Ammonia is trigonal pyramidal, with the lone pair on one side of the nitrogen. The N–H dipoles do not cancel.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of PCl5?
problems.why: Phosphorus has five bonds and no lone pair. The molecular shape is the same as the five-region geometry: trigonal bipyramidal.
hints: PCl5 has five bonds and no lone pair. The shape name is the five-region geometry itself.

problems.q: What is the bond angle in BF3, in degrees?
problems.why: BF3 has three bonding regions and no lone pair. They spread evenly in a plane, so the angle is 120°.
hints: BF3 has three regions and no lone pair, all in one plane. Divide a full circle by three.

problems.q: Is CCl4 polar or nonpolar?
problems.why: CCl4 is tetrahedral with four identical C–Cl bonds. The bond dipoles cancel, so CCl4 is nonpolar.
hints: Four identical outer atoms sit on a tetrahedron. Match this with CH4, not with CH3Cl.

problems.q: What is the molecular shape of SO2?
problems.why: Sulfur in SO2 has two bonding regions and one lone pair. Three regions with one lone pair give a bent molecular shape.
hints: SO2 has two S–O regions and one lone pair on sulfur. Three regions with one lone pair are not trigonal planar.
